extra.q: Write a valid CSS rule that makes all paragraphs blue.
extra.example: p is the selector. color is the property. blue is the value.

extra.q: Label each part in h1 { color: red; font-size: 20px; }.
extra.a:
Selector: h1.
Declarations: color: red and font-size: 20px.
Properties: color and font-size.
Values: red and 20px.
Curly braces surround declarations.
extra.example: selector { property: value; }

extra.q:
Write an ELEMENT selector that makes every

green.
extra.example: Element selector uses a tag name, with NO # or dot.

extra.q: Write a CLASS selector for HTML elements with class="important".
extra.example: Dot (.) means class. Many elements can share it.

extra.q: Write an ID selector for the element id="banner".
extra.example: Hash (#) means ID; use unique IDs on the page.

extra.q: Write an INLINE CSS example that colors a paragraph red.
extra.example: Inline styles are written inside that element’s style attribute.

extra.q: Write a short INTERNAL CSS example.
extra.example: Internal CSS uses <style> usually inside <head>.

extra.q: Link an EXTERNAL CSS file named style.css to an HTML page.
extra.example: External CSS is a separate .css file linked inside the HTML head.

extra.q: Draw and label the CSS box model from the inside out.
extra.a:
CONTENT → PADDING → BORDER → MARGIN.
Content is the text/image. Padding is space inside the border. Border surrounds padding. Margin is space outside the border.
extra.example: Picture four nested boxes. The margin is the outermost space.

extra.q: If width=200px, padding=10px on both sides, and border=5px on both sides, what is the total width?
extra.example: Margin is not counted in the border-box width.

extra.q: Rotate an element clockwise by 45 degrees using CSS.
extra.example: A positive angle rotates clockwise in the usual screen coordinate system.

extra.q: Make a box twice as wide without changing its height using transform.
extra.example: scaleX(2) = stretch in the X direction.

extra.q: Make an element half its original height using transform.
extra.example: scaleY changes the vertical size.

extra.q: Move an element 40px to the right using a 2D transform.
extra.example: Positive X = right; negative X = left.

extra.q: Make a left-to-right linear gradient from red to blue.
extra.example: Linear = colors change along a straight line.

extra.q: Make a circular radial gradient from white in the center to blue outside.
extra.example: Radial = colors spread outward from a center.

extra.q: What is JavaScript, and what job does it perform alongside HTML and CSS?
extra.a:
JavaScript is the scripting language that makes web pages interactive.
HTML = structure, CSS = appearance, JavaScript = behavior.
extra.example: A button that changes text after a click uses JavaScript.

extra.q: Write the simplest HTML page with JavaScript that logs Hello to the console.
extra.example: Use <script> for JavaScript in an HTML page.

extra.q: Explain the purpose of console.log() in one sentence.
extra.a: console.log() prints information to the browser developer console, mainly for testing and debugging.
extra.example: It does NOT display text in the web page itself.

extra.q: Which command changes the text inside the element whose id is result?
extra.example: getElementById FINDS the element; innerHTML CHANGES what is inside it.

extra.q: What is the difference between console.log("Hi") and alert("Hi")?
extra.a:
console.log("Hi") writes to the developer console.
alert("Hi") opens a popup alert box.
extra.example: They do not update a paragraph on the page.
x += 3 means x = x + 3.

extra.q:
Predict the output:
console.log("5" + 2);
extra.example: The quoted "5" is text, so + joins the strings rather than adding numbers.
10 > 5 is true, so the if block runs.

extra.q:
Predict the output:
for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { console.log(i); }
extra.example: Loop starts at 1, prints each value, stops after 3.

extra.q: Predict the content of the paragraph:
extra.example: JavaScript calculates 5 + 6 and writes it into the paragraph.

extra.q: Write an if–else that prints Adult when age is 18 or more, otherwise Minor.
extra.example: The if condition must be in parentheses.

extra.q: What does else if do? Give a small example.
extra.a:
else if checks another condition only when the earlier if or else if was false.
Example: if (mark >= 75) {...} else if (mark >= 50) {...} else {...}
extra.example: If / else if / else: first true branch wins.

extra.q: Write a for loop that prints the numbers 1, 2 and 3.
extra.example: Start i at 1; continue while i <= 3; increment i.

extra.q: Write a while loop that prints 1, 2 and 3.
extra.example: Update i inside the loop so it eventually stops.

extra.q: Write a do...while loop that prints 1 and 2.
extra.example: do...while always executes the body at least once.
The while condition is false before the first iteration.

extra.q: Write JavaScript switch code that prints Two for value 2, One for value 1, or Other.
extra.example: break prevents unintentionally continuing into the next case.
case 2 matches and break exits the switch.

extra.q: What happens if you forget break after a matching case in a JavaScript switch?
extra.a: Execution usually continues into the following case(s) until a break or the switch ends. This is called fall-through.
extra.example: Useful in some cases, but an easy exam mistake.

extra.q: Declare an array of three colors and print the second color.
extra.example: Arrays begin at index 0, so index 1 is the second element.
numbers[0] is 10; numbers[2] is 30.
Index 0 is the first element, not index 1.

extra.q: Write a function called greet that prints Hello when called.
extra.example: Define with function, then call using name followed by parentheses.

extra.q: Write a function add(a,b) that returns the sum and call it with 3 and 4.
extra.example: return sends a value back to the caller.

extra.q: What is the DOM, in simple words?
extra.a: DOM stands for Document Object Model. It represents the HTML page as objects/elements that JavaScript can find and change.
extra.example: Imagine the page as a tree of elements: html → body → p/button.

extra.q: What is the purpose of the DOM?
extra.a: It lets scripts access and update page content, properties, styles and elements, and respond to user actions.
extra.example: Click button → find paragraph with DOM → change the paragraph.
A string needs both opening and closing quotes.

extra.q:
Find and correct the syntax error:
if (x > 5 { console.log(x); }
extra.example: Missing closing ) after the condition.

extra.q:
Find the logic error: code should print 1, 2, 3.
for (let i = 1; i < 3; i++) { console.log(i); }
extra.a:
Use i <= 3 instead of i < 3.
for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { console.log(i); }
extra.example: i < 3 stops before printing 3.

extra.q:
Find the DOM error:

Hi
extra.example: The string passed to getElementById must match the HTML id exactly.

extra.q: Does forgetting one semicolon always cause an error in JavaScript?
extra.a: No. JavaScript often inserts missing semicolons automatically. But use them consistently, and watch for missing quotes/brackets or incorrect logic.
extra.example: A semicolon is good style; not every missing one is a syntax error.

extra.a:
Add i++ inside the while loop:
while (i <= 3) { console.log(i); i++; }
extra.example: Without increment, i stays 1 and the condition remains true.

extra.topic: Show a message in a paragraph
extra.q: Complete the HTML and JavaScript so the paragraph displays Welcome.
extra.example: HTML id and getElementById value must match.

extra.topic: Show a message in a paragraph
extra.q: Find the mistake:
extra.a:
innerHTML is a PROPERTY, not a function. Use = instead of parentheses:
document.getElementById("msg").innerHTML = "Hi";
extra.example: Property assignment uses =.

extra.q: In JavaScript, are "a" and "A" identical strings?
extra.a: No. JavaScript is case-sensitive, so lowercase "a" and uppercase "A" are different.
extra.example: "a" === "A" is false.

extra.q: Write JavaScript that converts lowercase a to uppercase A.
extra.example: toUpperCase() converts letters to capitals.
toUpperCase() makes capitals; toLowerCase() makes small letters.

extra.q: Write HTML code for a BULLETED list with Apple and Banana.
extra.example: ul = unordered list; li = list item.

extra.q: Write HTML code for a NUMBERED list with first and second steps.
extra.example: ol = ordered (numbered) list.

extra.q: Write a definition/description list for HTML: HyperText Markup Language.
extra.example: dl = description list; dt = term; dd = description.

extra.q: Write an HTML table with Name and Age headers, and one row for Ana, 19.
extra.example: tr = row; th = heading; td = normal cell.

extra.q:
What is wrong with this table?
AB
extra.a:
The cells need a table row ().
AB
extra.example: Put cells inside rows.

extra.q: What is the result of <th colspan="2">Results</th>?
extra.a: One header cell spans TWO columns instead of one.
extra.example: colspan combines columns; rowspan combines rows.
